note: Netcode was the largest cost: about 2,900 of 6,800 lines (lobby, sessions, input buffering, snapshots, prediction, reconciliation, bot takeover, telemetry) written from scratch because DedicatedServer serves walking characters.
workaround: Implement NetGame + ClientView and use viewer::netplay (docs/NETPLAY.md); do not write a server.
hint: Implement NetGame + ClientView on viewer::netplay (docs/NETPLAY.md); do not write a server or lobby.

note: The engine speaks JSON, which does not fit 8 karts in one datagram; a bounds-checked binary reader/writer and fuzz test were hand-written.
workaround: Use net::codec::{Writer, Reader} (fuzz-tested).
hint: Use net::codec::{Writer, Reader} for datagram snapshots; do not hand-write a binary codec.

note: A Template over 9,000 vertices was skipped by Batch::add with no message and the whole world vanished (a debugging round).
trap: Meshes over the vertex limit vanish silently; Template::split and Batch::add now split them, but a hand-made window must also raise the draw-call capacity (game_client::window_config).
hint: Oversize meshes vanish silently: use game_client::window_config and Template::split.

note: Template::quad needs counter-clockwise corners seen from the front; the wrong order is culled with no hint (a debugging round).
workaround: Use Template::quad_facing(normal), which winds the quad to face a normal.
trap: A wrongly wound quad is culled silently.
hint: A wrongly wound quad is culled silently: use Template::quad_facing(normal).

note: Finding APIs meant reading engine source (Lifecycle::feed, ScriptFrame::held vs starts, Template::cone argument order, sound presets, GamepadFrame, MenuStep); context named files, not signatures; dozens of tool calls.
workaround: Read docs/CUSTOM_SIM_CHEATSHEET.md first; be2.py context lists public_api names.
hint: Read docs/CUSTOM_SIM_CHEATSHEET.md before grepping the engine source.

note: No xvfb recipe was documented and software rendering ran at about 16 frames per second (a full race took 7.5 minutes to capture).
workaround: python tools/xcapture.py and docs/HEADLESS_CAPTURE.md.
hint: Headless screenshots: python tools/xcapture.py (docs/HEADLESS_CAPTURE.md); software GL is slow.

note: Papercuts: scripts/blue called python (this box has python3), check.py demanded BE2_TOOLS, the first cargo command must not use --locked, new-game argument order is easy to get wrong.
hint: Use python3 with the scripts; the first cargo build must not use --locked.

note: A closed track/spline with arc length, nearest point and lateral offset (src/track.rs) is something every racing or patrol game rebuilds.
workaround: Use devkit::path::ClosedPath (progress, lateral offset, arc distance, yaw helpers).
hint: Use devkit::path::ClosedPath for track progress, lateral offset and arc distance.

note: Testing netcode needed an in-memory network with delay, jitter and loss; the engine NetworkSimulator only handled its own Packet type.
workaround: Use net::loopback::LoopNet for raw datagrams.
hint: Test lossy networks with net::loopback::LoopNet instead of real sockets.

note: GameShell::playing() is false without a captured mouse; Spooky Kart gated race input on it and shipped with every key dead while menus worked; scripted runs bypass the gate so no test saw it.
workaround: Gate input on GameShell::accepting_input().
trap: GameShell::playing() needs a captured mouse; scripted and autopilot runs cannot catch a dead gate.
hint: Gate input on GameShell::accepting_input(); playing() is false without a captured mouse.

note: On Windows the native key reader polled a 23-key shortlist: R, digits, G, Tab and most letters were never pressed in custom-sim games (Spooky Kart, Deadfall) while every Linux test passed.
workaround: Build on an engine with the full game_input::KEY_TABLE; check --windows type-checks cfg(windows) code.
trap: Windows native input once read only 23 keys; any other key was silently dead on Windows only.
hint: Windows-only dead keys fixed in 1e2d2bc: rebuild; check --windows type-checks cfg(windows) code.

note: ClientState::Rejected("Could not reach the server") read like a refusal when nobody had answered.
workaround: Show NetClient::failure().hint() to the player (docs/NETPLAY.md, When connecting fails).
trap: A silent server looked like a refusal.
hint: Use NetClient::failure().hint() to tell the player why connecting failed.

note: Games hand-rolled server-address entry with no paste and no default address.
workaround: Use devkit::TextField, resolve_ipv4 and the default-server chain (server.txt).
hint: Use devkit::TextField (paste), resolve_ipv4 and the server.txt default-server chain.

note: The dedicated-server main (args, join key, report dir, transport choice) is about 65 lines identical modulo names in prop-hunt, slapstick and spooky-kart, and rewritten for deadfall.
workaround: Use netplay::cli::serve and ServeSpec for the dedicated server main.
hint: Dedicated server main: netplay::cli::serve + ServeSpec (docs/NETPLAY.md).

note: Every game builds its own lobby hub to find and join matches; there is no shared hub or room browser.
hint: Room browser and matchmaking: netplay::hub::client on the shared be2-hub (docs/NETPLAY.md).
workaround: Use the shared be2-hub and netplay::hub::client for room discovery and Play Online.

note: Kit games had no shadows: flat look, and each game would have written its own.
workaround: kit::Shadows with devkit::ShadowQuality (Off/Simple/Full, --shadows); Batch::blob for contact shadows.
hint: Shadows: kit::Shadows + devkit::ShadowQuality (Off/Simple/Full); Batch::blob for contact blobs.

note: Kerb stripes at y = 0 sat on the road quad and z-fought, which surface won changing with the camera; no engine test could see it.
workaround: Lift the upper one or run kit::lint::lint (CoplanarOverlap); lint::depth_resolution(near, distance).
trap: Two same-facing surfaces in one plane z-fight.
hint: Same-plane surfaces z-fight: lift the upper one or run kit::lint::lint (CoplanarOverlap).

note: The road border offset each sample along its own segment normal; at a tight bend the strip turned inside out.
workaround: Template::offset_strip (mitred, curvature-clamped); lint::strip_folds checks any strip.
trap: Per-segment-normal offsets fold at tight bends.
hint: Use Template::offset_strip for road borders and lint::strip_folds to check them.

note: fx_alpha and fx_add are never depth-tested: miniquad enables the depth test only when depth_write is true, so translucent marks and glass showed through walls.
workaround: Use Materials::decal (depth-tested, biased) or Batch::blob / kit::Shadows.
trap: fx_alpha/fx_add ignore depth; a flat translucent mark shows through walls and over cars.
hint: fx_alpha/fx_add ignore depth: use Materials::decal or Batch::blob for depth-tested translucent marks.

note: A far/near ratio of 7000 leaves about 6 mm of depth resolution at 100 m, so distant coplanar-ish details fight no matter how they were lifted.
workaround: Keep far/near under about 3000 (raise near); View::camera_checked warns once.
hint: Keep camera far/near under about 3000; View::camera_checked warns.

note: Shadow rendering on miniquad: render_target_ex is RGBA8 with an unreadable depth, sample_count 1 blits after every draw, Linear filtering corrupts packed depth, sampler2D is lowp, GLSL 100 has no dFdx.
workaround: Copy kit::shadow rather than re-deriving it.
hint: Copy kit::shadow for shadow maps; do not re-derive the miniquad render-target workarounds.

note: Weapon and soldier models needed lofts, sweeps, rounded boxes and mirroring; two helper agents each wrote their own (about 1,500 lines in two files). A toolkit would have saved about 30% of the art tokens (estimate).
workaround: Use kit::shape: Template::loft, sweep, rounded_box, capsule, mirror_x, smooth_normals.
hint: Use kit::shape (Template::loft, sweep, rounded_box, capsule, mirror_x) for models; do not write lofts.

note: Three redo passes after feedback (weapon models 353k, soldier bodies 165k, hands 221k) cost 739,352 tokens (30% of the build) and about an hour; the first versions were too blocky.
workaround: Have the shape toolkit before the first model, not after the first complaint.
hint: Build the shape toolkit before the first model: redo passes cost Deadfall 30% of its tokens.

note: Art was 67% of about 2.44M tokens: weapons 683k in two passes, the map 360k, soldiers 366k, hands 221k. Procedural modelling without textures or imports means every look decision is code plus a screenshot loop.
workaround: Shape toolkit exists now; there is still no glTF/OBJ import and no model preview tool.
hint: Art was 67% of Deadfall's tokens; there is no model import or preview tool.

note: The lead agent read the netplay kit, kit renderer, Controller, audio and release scripts as source (about 110,000 tokens) because no document says how a networked shooter fits together.
workaround: docs/NETPLAY.md and the cheat sheet cover the kit pieces, not the shooter architecture.
hint: No document covers a networked shooter end to end; expect to read the netplay kit source.

note: SoundBank::play(index, volume) has no pan, pitch or distance: every directional sound was rendered as 7 pre-panned stereo copies (154 MB decoded) and automatic-weapon shots are bit-identical repeats.
workaround: Pre-pan variants per direction.
hint: Live spatial/pitch voices remain unsupported; AudioProject scores can bake stereo pan.

note: First-person weapons poke through walls without their own depth pass; there is no depth-only clear, so a render target was used.
workaround: Draw the viewmodel into a render target.
hint: First-person viewmodels clip through walls: draw them into a separate render target.

note: A game window without game_client::window_config lacks draw_call_vertex_capacity: 30000, so meshes above macroquad 10,000 vertices / 5,000 indices are dropped silently; three helper agents lost time to missing geometry.
workaround: Build the window from game_client::window_config.
trap: A hand-made macroquad Conf drops big meshes silently.
hint: Build the window from game_client::window_config or big meshes are dropped silently.

note: No way to inject key, mouse or controller events through the real input path, so scripted input bypasses exactly the gate that broke Spooky Kart and no agent can verify controls on a real window.
hint: No injection of real key, mouse or controller events: scripted runs skip the input gate.

note: No local Windows verification: a Windows compile error cost a 20-25 minute CI round trip for the whole release workflow (every game builds).
workaround: python tools/be2.py check --windows (cargo check for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu; compiles, does not run).
hint: check --windows type-checks cfg(windows) code locally; it runs nothing.

note: NetGame::start(seed, seats, participants) is a static fn with no configuration: match rules (kill limit, time, bots) reached it through a process-global, which blocks one process serving several rooms with different rules.
trap: Process-global match settings make a multi-room server share one set of rules.
hint: NetGame::start has no config: match rules via a process-global break multi-room servers.

note: One choice: u8 per seat and no lobby data of your own: team balance, "team full", host rules and joining a match in progress are not possible in the kit.
hint: The lobby has one choice: u8 per seat: no team-full state and no join in progress.

note: Lag compensation (net::lag_compensation, PoseHistory) was not indexed and is still not documented for NetGame games; Deadfall rewrote pose history and rewind (seen_tick) for hit registration and killcam.
workaround: Indexed as feature lag_compensation; read src/viewer/net/lag_compensation.rs and docs/NETPLAY.md.
hint: Lag compensation (PoseHistory) is in src/viewer/net/lag_compensation.rs; not yet in docs/NETPLAY.md.

note: pathing is 2D/room-graph; Deadfall wrote a 3D multi-floor navigation graph (about 300 lines) with its own stair-tread bug (a 0.5 m grid is coarser than 0.3 m treads).
workaround: devkit::waypoints covers a branching graph with shortest path, not stairs.
hint: devkit::waypoints is a graph plus shortest path; no 3D multi-floor or stair support.

note: The custom-sim scaffold ships a complete single-player game that has to be deleted; its identity smoke args assume --exit-after, which only Lifecycle games implement.
hint: The custom-sim scaffold ships a full demo game to delete; there is no --empty option.

note: Lifecycle (flags, fixed step, --capture, --script, --frames) is tied to Sim/Held; a networked game with its own loop reimplements them.
hint: Lifecycle flags (--capture, --script, --frames) are tied to Sim/Held.

note: An interactable needed four matching records in map.json (material, node, collider, entity) and validation failed on any mismatch; found by trial and error in all ten games.
workaround: be2-tools add-interactable GAME.json ID --at=X,Y,Z --write creates all of them in one validated step.
hint: Use be2-tools add-interactable to create all the matching map records in one step.

note: Rule conditions only tested counter == n and the only outcome was complete, so no timer could lose the game (a countdown reached -3 and the player still won).
workaround: Use fail and the richer conditions (comparisons, modulo, all/any/not).
hint: Rules can fail and compare: use fail and comparison, modulo, all/any/not conditions.

note: A timer written with interval_ticks or period_ticks is rejected; only duration_ticks, auto_start and repeats are accepted.
trap: Timer field is duration_ticks, not interval_ticks.
hint: Timers take duration_ticks (not interval_ticks), auto_start and repeats.

note: Rules are limited to 4 actions (limits.actions_per_rule); complex resets need daisy-chained counter triggers.
hint: Rules allow at most 4 actions (actions_per_rule); chain counters for more.

note: Doorway gaps in straight walls and a branching waypoint graph with shortest path were hand-built for one game and had no game-specific content.
workaround: devkit::level::wall_along_x / wall_along_z and devkit::waypoints.
hint: Use devkit::level::wall_along_x/z for doorway gaps and devkit::waypoints for room paths.

note: Drawing static meshes with draw_mesh before gl_use_material(&materials.world) compiles, runs and renders an empty scene: no error or warning; found only by inspecting a capture.
trap: draw_mesh before gl_use_material(&materials.world) draws nothing and says nothing.
hint: Call gl_use_material(&materials.world) before draw_mesh or the scene renders empty.

note: Dead Air hand-derived direction.0.atan2(-direction.2) to face its monster toward the player; devkit::path::yaw_of already did exactly that: a discoverability gap.
workaround: Use devkit::path::yaw_of(direction) (yaw 0 faces -Z) and wrap_angle.
hint: Face a target with devkit::path::yaw_of(direction); yaw 0 faces -Z.

note: physics.rs (Physics, Body, Material over rapier, about 350 lines) is byte-identical in tumble-maze, wobble-tower and clockwork-pinball; the engine has no equivalent (dupes: 3 copies x 216 normalised lines).
hint: physics.rs (Physics/Body/Material over rapier) is copied in 3 games; the engine has no equivalent yet.

note: Bot clients (bin/*-bots.rs: connect N NetClient bots and drive them) share about 55 lines across prop-hunt, slapstick and spooky-kart (dupes).
hint: Bot-client mains (*-bots.rs) are copied in 3 games; there is no engine helper yet.

note: Each game invented its own "press R to restart after game over" handling.
workaround: Use ClientInput::restart_requested(game_over) (the shared convention).
hint: Use ClientInput::restart_requested(game_over) for the R-to-restart convention.

note: No reset/step/observe/reward interface, trajectory recorder or external-process control exists for AI agents; the external study sketches a PettingZoo-style env to define with the first real consumer.
hint: No reset/step/observe/reward interface for agents exists yet.

note: Two engine tests failed the gate on a busy machine: the hub tests collided on a port when another suite ran at once, and the zombie test gave a spawned program only one second.
trap: Tests that pick ports or wait on a process must tolerate several suites running together on one machine.
hint: Run one test suite at a time; port pickers need clock-mixed seeds and process waits need seconds, not ms.

note: Typing the letter F in a game text box (Spooky Kart room name) toggles fullscreen, because the engine shell treats F as a hotkey while a text field has focus.
workaround: ClientInput::feed_text / text_input_active() mask the F hotkey while a field is focused.
trap: Shell hotkeys fire while typing: mask shell actions while a TextField has focus.
hint: Typing F is safe now: feed_text (or text_input_active) masks the fullscreen hotkey.

note: Many parallel agents each used their own cargo target dir and the shared engine cache grew to over 30 GB; the disk hit 97% and builds risked failing.
workaround: One shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR per repo, delete regenerable profiles (itest, debug) between phases.
trap: Parallel build agents exhaust disk: share one target dir and prune it.
hint: Share one CARGO_TARGET_DIR across agents and prune itest/debug profiles; check df before big builds.

note: Another session had already fixed the same six Deadfall issues on origin/main while this session redid them, so the duplicate fixes were discarded.
trap: Another session may already have pushed the same fix: fetch and read origin/main before starting.
hint: git fetch and read origin/main's log before fixing a game: another session may already have.

note: Four netplay games each copied a ~65-line server main and Deadfall had its own hub; now one cli::serve and one multi-game be2-hub serve every game (ADR 0037).
workaround: Set NetGame::MAX_SEATS for join capacity; use netplay::cli::serve for the server and netplay::hub::client for Play Online.
hint: Player cap: NetGame::MAX_SEATS. Server: netplay::cli::serve; rooms: netplay::hub (ADR 0037).

note: A retired room's server died with a 'failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe' panic (exit 101) because println! panics when the hub has closed its status pipe.
workaround: Print progress through netplay::say, which ignores a closed pipe.
trap: println! panics on a broken pipe: a supervised process must not use it for progress lines.
hint: Supervised servers must not println!: use netplay::say, a closed pipe panics println!.

note: Loopback test ports were picked in 43000-44999, inside Linux's ephemeral range 32768-60999, so client sockets could take a reserved port; the hub tests failed the gate intermittently.
workaround: Pick test ports below 32768 (hub tests now use 25000-26899).
trap: Test ports inside the ephemeral range collide with port-0 sockets: use ports below 32768.
hint: Pick loopback test ports below 32768; the ephemeral range 32768-60999 collides with port-0 clients.

note: Fractional box translations rounded visual and collision bounds differently; canonical apply now preserves exact agreement for already matching selected records.
workaround: Create controls with add-interactable; translate node, collider and entity together, then game-validate.
hint: Use add-interactable, then canonical translate selecting node/collider/entity together; game-validate.

note: Direct movement failed behind gates and turning obstacles; overdue repeated interactions coalesced after walks. Routed walks and executed-step holds now verify the chosen physical run.
hint: Use route:true on walk_to and wait_ticks:1 on each repeated press; verify with sim, then --scenario capture.

note: Rejected-source rollback memory skipped incomplete activation. Ordinary updates now verify the restored artifact and resume installation, activation and readiness without rebuilding rejected source.
hint: Retry ordinary update after incomplete rollback: verified restored artifacts resume activation/readiness.

note: Static map lint cannot prove later access through a changing shutter. Game-aware lint now retains initial findings and resolves only targets individually observed in a verified shared-simulation scenario.
hint: For gates use lint MAP --game=GAME --scenario=WIN: only physically observed targets resolve initial errors.

note: CI used unoptimized dev tests and separate profile builds. Canonical itest gates now reuse build artifacts and cached dependencies; one reviewed independent Python batch overlaps serial Cargo, while native integration stays ordered.
hint: Use be2.py check for canonical itest gates; perf.py record --suite check measures stages in one full run.

note: Rapid Windows game checks reused a wall-clock timestamp and collided before verification. Engine and generated-game checks now reserve unique report directories atomically, preserving earlier failure logs.
hint: Copy templates/game_check.py to game scripts/check.py for timestamp-safe reports; prior logs survive.

note: Audio cues required Rust recipes and numeric indices; named JSON projects now render reusable checked stereo bundles. Edit scores, instruments, variants and adaptive layers without recompiling or synthesizing music at startup. Numeric quality and decoder readiness remain separate from perceived quality and device audibility.
hint: Use be2-tools audio describe/render/check; load named bundles with kit::AudioBank.

note: Stock GameDocument audio needed a supported runtime path beyond a standalone preview; presentation.audio now loads checked named bundles and observes confirmed state transitions.
hint: Stock audio: presentation.audio binds checked bundles to state cues/music; see docs/AUDIO.md.

note: Endless walking needs bounded chunk streaming and local coordinates, not a growing map with global f32 positions.
hint: Use devkit::procedural for seeded chunks, local coordinates, bounded streaming and DayCycle.

note: Field-recorded ambience needed exact named adaptive loops without duplicating WAV conversion or runtime synthesis.
hint: AudioProject music kind clips crossfades imported PCM loops; Leo shows recorded nature and an authored score.

note: A source-tree capture loaded ambience successfully while the shipped game omitted its audio assets.
hint: Package runtime banks in identity.package; capture the shipped executable without a source asset override.

note: A package beside its checkout can hide missing assets through working-directory or source fallback. Smoke now stages only stamped payload, verifies hashes and uses fresh player state; runtime_assets forbids source fallback for packaged games.
Shipping checked only exe hash and directory presence; stale dist/ files could satisfy runtime smoke. Added every-file integrity, stock map closure and declared-file isolated smoke.
trap: Source/dist assets can hide incomplete packages.
hint: verify checks hashes without a display; --smoke launches only declared files outside the checkout.

note: Capture runs mute SoundBank and can pass without generating/loading audio. Added --audible opt-in and AudioStatus failure/load/playback evidence. Numeric analysis found a real ambient chord-tail cutoff; shared synth now fades finite tails.
trap: Silent capture success does not verify audio.
hint: Use --audible and SoundBank::status counts; a null device still needs a listening check.

note: Building the overview game exposed keyboard/pad settings rows that could not be activated. Shared GameShell now navigates only available settings and keeps the screen open on toggles; real captures and persistent settings checked.
trap: A settings screen can render but be unusable from keyboard/pad.
hint: GameShell settings rows now accept Up/Down and Enter/A; capture scripts use ShellActions.

note: A modification added a shield field to saved/hashed state. The real version-one fixture migrates and completes its original route. Corrected save docs: serde default alone cannot fix Exact hash changes.
trap: New saved fields can deserialize yet fail Exact state hash checks.
hint: Bump Snapshot::VERSION and migrate when state_hash changes, even with serde default.

note: Creation read the custom-sim starter and cheat sheet. Modification needed game AGENTS, lib and rules tests plus main/audio for cues; no engine internals. Shipping script refresh still requires a manual copy from the engine template.
trap: Already generated shipping scripts do not inherit engine fixes automatically.
hint: Upgrade plan plus refresh templates/game_ship.py, then rerun the game project and package checks.

note: The normal Linux scripts/blue ship command failed with Permission denied: the scaffold never marked scripts/blue executable. Fixed Unix mode in newgame and tested direct launcher execution. Also repaired copied Bash PY spelling in PowerShell play.
trap: A generated launcher can exist yet fail the documented command.
hint: new-game now creates an executable scripts/blue; PowerShell play uses python.

note: author.py describe expected bin/be2-tools despite be2.py build tools using target/be2-tools/release. Added source-checkout discovery with explicit override preserved; a fresh agent can now run describe without manually copying a binary.
trap: Build tools output and discovery path can disagree.
hint: author.py describe discovers the be2.py build tools output; BE2_TOOLS remains an explicit override.

note: The first game duplicated an end-of-run audio proof predicate. Added AudioStatus::verify_playback with expected bank counts, and wired the custom-sim starter so --audible cannot quietly certify an unloaded or unplayed bank.
trap: ready() alone means loading ended; it does not mean every cue loaded or played.
hint: SoundBank::status().verify_playback(expected_variants, expected_stems) fails incomplete audio checks.

note: The final archived audible capture failed because xcapture always inserted --mute. The audio gate rejected it correctly. Capture helper now omits implicit mute for --audible, retains explicit mute precedence, and forwards executable verification reports.
trap: A screenshot helper can accidentally suppress the audio path requested by an agent.
hint: xcapture -- --audible exercises audio and retains runtime evidence; explicit --mute still wins.

note: Real WASM load exposed stale Macroquad bundled JavaScript versus locked Miniquad. Shared web build assembles the loader from exact dependency sources and rejects missing imports instead of installing silent stubs.
trap: Compiling WASM does not prove loader ABI compatibility.
hint: Use web build: exact locked JS loader imports are checked by a real isolated browser.

note: New save/settings notices added glyphs after queued draws and invalidated Macroquad font atlas textures. Shared Scene drawing now preloads all glyphs before submitting primitives/text.
trap: A static initial capture can miss later UI font failures.
hint: Browser smoke exercises save/settings notices as well as the first game frame.

note: Fresh external starter failed locked tests because cargo metadata --no-deps did not settle its seeded lock. Shared web build now resolves the seeded pins with full offline metadata before locked tests/builds.
hint: The two-d web build settles seeded locks offline; Cargo compilation alone is not browser verification.

note: Mobile Start on touch-down could finish an accelerated route before browser audio activated. Digital Start now runs on touch release; a separate real-touch audio gate catches it.

3D camera viewports used physical pixels while the 2D logical canvas used device-scaled pixels. Emulated mobile screenshots exposed misaligned tiny 3D views; shared DPI conversion and regression now align both.

Touch controls below the canvas scrolled away when activating canvas focus. Focus now prevents scrolling; portrait and landscape tests reach real controls. Unified catalog integration preserves newer installers and version pages.

Leo reuses its original Sim, Snapshot and art through the portable browser client. Shared checked loop banks and read-only render_view avoid duplicated platform code. Replay batches preserve exact hashes. Real direction probes hold input until gameplay responds, independent of slow software-GPU frames. F fullscreen must run inside a trusted key gesture.
trap: A brief direction probe may end before a slow renderer observes it; WASM compilation alone does not verify input.

note: Browser publication must anonymously fetch exact source and reproduce in an empty target. Cargo source hashes must ignore Python caches; WASM paths need remapping; audio bank packaging follows referenced PCM rather than copying preview mixes.
trap: A locally successful browser build can claim an unavailable public revision or depend on development artifacts; publish always performs clean reproduction.
